P1-SIM-03 — COMBAT REPLAY DOES NOT RESTORE THE COMPLETE INITIAL SCENE **Finding:** Confirmed by source inspection. Files: ```text scripts/sim/combat_actor_state.gd:222–270 scripts/sim/combat_scenario.gd:91–120 scripts/sim/combat_scenario.gd:249–280 ``` `CombatActorState.snapshot()` records: ```text position velocity yaw_rad radius ``` But `restore_snapshot()` restores health, shield, ammo, energy and active effects without restoring these spatial fields. It also does not restore the full hitbox representation. ## Consequence After a target moves or rotates, calling: ```gdscript reset("ALL") ``` does not necessarily restore its original position, velocity or collision geometry. `replay_deterministic()` consequently may use a different scene state than the original experiment. ## Additional replay limitation `shot_history` records: ```text origin direction target_position shooter_velocity weapon_name ordnance_name ammo_spent energy_spent time ``` But replay uses the *current* WeaponProfile and externally supplied obstacles rather than an immutable snapshot of every historical shot's relevant configuration. This limits replay across: - ODF edits. - Weapon changes. - Target movement. - Obstacle changes. - Multiple actors. ## Required fix Introduce an immutable CombatReplaySnapshot containing: ```text Scenario ID Simulation seed Initial actor states Actor transforms Hitboxes Obstacles Selected ODF revisions Weapon profiles Projectile parameters Timeline input events Shot commands ``` Restore the complete initial scene before replay. Avoid overwriting the current user's scenario unexpectedly when replaying an old experiment. Prefer a sandboxed replay instance or provide an explicit destructive reset policy. ## Acceptance ```text Target starts at X=0 Shot 1 Move target to X=20 Shot 2 Replay ``` The replay must reproduce the intended historical sequence, including the move. After changing the ODF, replaying the old run must still use the old captured revision. A new run may use the newly edited ODF. This distinction is essential for meaningful A/B comparisons. --- # 10. P1-SIM-04 — RECONFIGURATION OVERWRITES THE REPLAY BASELINE **Finding:** Confirmed source behavior; user-visible consequences need regression tests. File: ```text scripts/sim/combat_scenario.gd:25–70 ``` `configure_from_profile()` recreates the shooter and primary target, optionally preserving current ammo/energy/hull/shield. Then it always calls: ```gdscript capture_initial_snapshots() ``` If the scenario has already fired multiple shots, `preserve_state=true` carries depleted values into the newly captured baseline. Thus the meaning of “initial scenario” can change during a weapon/profile update. Also, recreating the actors can discard: - Reload state. - Active status effects. - Other transient actor state. ## Required fix Separate: ```text CREATE NEW SCENARIO UPDATE EFFECTIVE ODF PARAMETERS CHANGE WEAPON RESET TO INITIAL CAPTURE REPLAY BASELINE ``` These are different operations. A routine parameter refresh must not silently redefine the initial combat state. When changing weapon profile during an ongoing experiment: - Preserve actor resources where appropriate. - Preserve active effects. - Preserve elapsed cooldown when semantically applicable. - Record the profile change as a timeline event. - Keep the original replay baseline intact. ## Acceptance ```text Initial ammo: 30 Fire → 20 Edit weapon parameter Fire → 10 Reset to initial ``` Expected: ```text Ammo restored to 30 ``` not to 20.
